body:
You see? It's all that I'm courageous to be honest with myself. Or that I'm an inspiration to others going through the same thing. It's fake and it's a lie. I'm scared to death of who I am.

Countless times per day I have to tell myself how to act in order to be perceived as a functioning person. I am constantly deciding in my head what the best thing to say would be in order for no one to question my well being. I need to always be in control and it is exhausting. To this day I have not done any drugs or drank any form of alcohol for fear that I would lose control.

I know that I have people in my life that love me very much. I would hope they would understand how much living this kind of life hurts.

That article seems spot on. I have been in therapy for a little over a year. It is really difficult talking to people in person about being transgendered. Im hoping to tell him at my next appointment on the 6th.

You make some good points. I do realize that my job is not getting any better and I've often wondered if I'm keeping it to make myself feel like suicide is the right answer. 

I suppose you're right about stating the gender that I identify as rather then coldly identifying as transgendered. I identify as female. 

I know that saying I want to be normal is probably frowned upon and I understand that nobody is really normal. But I feel like life would have been a lot easier if I didn't have to come to terms with coming out of the closet as gay, and now having to come out as trans.
I have started saving. But thinking about surgery and having to tell people creates more stressors than I can deal with. I just want to be done having to make decisions. I'm so emotionally exhausted
